theorem_title: Canonical-word legality of the thirteen unlabelled YAH rows
natural_language_statement:
Let $R$ be the fixed list of thirteen unlabelled YAH rule instances. For a row $r$, let $L_r$ and $R_r$ be its left and right words after inserting its stored prefix and suffix. A word is canonical when it starts with $\hat{}$, ends with $\$$, and has only the five digit symbols $f,t,0,1,2$ in its interior. Then

$$\forall r\in R,\quad \operatorname{canonical}(L_r)\land\operatorname{canonical}(R_r).$$

This checks the syntactic domain of the displayed finite certificate rows. The statement is restricted to this list of instances.
